observation: Original sets the page background to a saturated red-orange (rgb 213,68,39), with a duotone skyline photo tinted behind the header and the top of the hero. The AI-built page uses a white body background and separates bands with full-width pale mint tints.

Original's palette is red-orange, white and near-black (#1f1f1f), with one lime green background, #333 body text and #666 dates. The AI-built page's palette is white, pale mint (238,244,241), deep green (11,107,85) and dark teal-black (21,41,43), with grey (92,111,113) secondary text.

The accent color differs. Original reuses its brand orange for link text, the 'Read More' accent and the page background (24 text uses). The AI-built page uses deep green (16 text uses) for links, buttons and eyebrow labels.

Both pages center a fixed-width content column in a 1440px viewport. Original's column is about 1200px (x120–1320), with modules floating on the orange field. The AI-built page's column is about 1068px (x186–1254), inside full-bleed section bands.

Both pages put the featured hero in two columns, but the content differs. Original has a large 835px photo with a dark caption on the left and a white 'Latest News' sidebar on the right. The AI-built page has a 538px photo on the left and a text stack (eyebrow, date, h1, Read More button) on the right, on a tinted band. Latest News moves to its own section below.

Both pages use the same documentary photo of a protester holding a red 'Asijiki!' sign (835x557 source). Original renders it at full 835x557 size with square corners and empty alt, with a dark gradient fading into a #1f1f1f caption panel. The AI-built page renders it at 538x359 with slightly rounded corners and the alt 'Featured commentary photo'.

Original's hero headline is white text of about 30px in regular weight, sitting in the dark caption and followed inline by an orange 'Read More' at the same size. The AI-built page's hero headline is a 35.2px bold dark-teal h1 in a ~490px column, followed by a separate solid green 'Read More' button.
Original's h1 is empty, so the logo is the only title-like element. The AI-built page's h1 carries the featured commentary headline.
The AI-built page puts a small uppercase, letter-spaced eyebrow label ('FEATURED COMMENTARY' in green, 'MANAGING PARTNER' in grey) above content.

Original uses the proxima-nova webfont (169 elements), paired with italic Georgia serif for module headings (6 elements). The AI-built page uses only a system-ui sans stack (107 elements) plus Arial (2), with no serif and no webfont.
The heading scale differs. Original's h2 is 28px/500, and its module headings are small italic serif. The AI-built page's h2 is 25.6px/700 bold sans, and its h3 article titles are bold.
Both pages use 16px body text. Original has a tight 20px line height. The AI-built page uses 25.6px (1.6).

Original's logo is a white-caps text-style wordmark with mixed weights and a tagline, sitting on the tinted skyline; its logo img reports a 0x0 rect. The AI-built page shows logo.png at 401x52 at the left of the header with alt text, but it looks blank or very light in the screenshot.

The header layout differs. Original has the logo with a large, widely spaced row of white unbolded nav links below it (About, News, Publications, Contact Us), and no nav element. The AI-built page has a single-row header: logo at left, dark bold nav links inside a nav element, then search and Sign Up grouped at right, with a thin bottom border.

Both pages put a search field and a sign-up entry at the top right. Original uses a Search input with a thin underline and a grey icon, plus a 'Get the Newsletter' link with an icon; 'Search form' and 'Sign Up' are h2s. The AI-built page uses a visually hidden label, an input with 'Search' placeholder text, an icon-only magnifier button and a solid green 'Sign Up' button.

Latest News has three dated items in both pages. Original shows them as a vertical sidebar list with grey dates, orange headline links ending in '›', hairline dividers and 'All news ›' at the bottom. The AI-built page shows them as a three-column ul/li grid of cards, each with a 3px green top rule, a grey time date and a bold h3 link, with 'All news →' at the right of the section header.

The secondary modules are laid out differently. Original has a row of three equal-width cards: a dark Video card, a white Upcoming Events card and a white Recent Tweets card. The AI-built page gives Videos its own section, then puts Events and Recent Tweets in two unequal columns (443px and 577px).
On both pages the Events module is mostly empty, holding only a heading and a 'See Past Events' link; the AI-built page also adds a grey line, 'No upcoming events at the moment.'

Both pages show a featured video thumbnail with a baked-in player control bar plus two further video links. Original puts them in a dark card, marking the featured video with a large white ring-and-chevron overlay and the other two links with smaller grey ring icons. The AI-built page uses a 586px thumbnail at left with a two-item hairline-divided text list at right and no ring icons, leaving empty space below the list.

Original uses a dark #1f1f1f treatment for two modules: the hero caption and the Video card, whose white italic serif heading sits on the dark ground. The AI-built page has no dark content modules; its only dark band is the footer.

Both pages show Recent Tweets as static text with no avatars or embeds, with links for handles and t.co URLs and grey relative timestamps like '2 days 21 hours ago'. Original colors the links orange and shows an empty left indent. The AI-built page colors them green and underlined, in a ul list with hairline dividers.

Both pages show the WRI managing partner, Coalition for Urban Transitions and FOLU logos with an 'All partners' link. Original uses a white band with an italic serif and bold sans 'Managing Partner' label and a vertical divider. The AI-built page uses three bordered white cards of different widths on a tinted band, with an uppercase 'MANAGING PARTNER' eyebrow and full-color logos at about 70px high, leaving empty space to the right.
Careers appears differently. Original has a plain 'Careers ›' text link at the left of the footer. The AI-built page has a dedicated centered section with an h2 and a green 'View careers' button.

The footer differs. Original's minimal footer sits on the orange background with no footer element and has 'Careers ›' plus 'Connect' with dark brown social glyphs. The AI-built page uses a dark teal-black footer element band with a copyright line and five white circular social icon badges (YouTube, LinkedIn, G+, Facebook, Twitter) as 24px PNGs with empty alt.
Both pages use a flat visual language with no transitions, animations, transforms or backdrop blur. Original adds 1 box shadow and 2 gradient backgrounds. The AI-built page has none of either.
Corner radii differ. Every element on Original has radius 0 (180 elements). The AI-built page is mostly square (95 elements) but has 9 small 1–7px radii and 5 pill or circle shapes.

Original has no buttons (buttons 0, primary_button null) and uses only text links. The AI-built page adds solid green rectangular buttons with white bold text ('Read More', 'Sign Up', 'View careers').
Both pages use arrow-suffixed text links ('All news', 'See Past Events', 'All partners'). Original uses a '›' chevron in orange. The AI-built page uses a '→' arrow in green.
Original prefixes headlines with 'Commentary:' and sets them in title case. The AI-built page drops the prefix and uses sentence-case headlines.
Both pages put long-form dates ('April 14, 2021') in time elements, in smaller grey text above headlines: 6 time elements on Original, 4 on the AI-built page.

Semantics differ. Original is div-heavy (69 divs), with 6 header and 8 article elements and no nav, main, section or footer. The AI-built page has one header, nav, main and footer plus 6 section elements, and no article elements, so news items are li.
Original's heading outline includes utility h2s ('Search form', 'Sign Up') and 14 h2s in total. The AI-built page has a clean outline: one h1, 6 h2s and 3 h3s.

No image on either page is missing an alt attribute, and decorative or some images use empty alt. Original has no ARIA attributes and leaves the hero alt empty. The AI-built page has 7 ARIA attributes and descriptive alts on content images, across 12 images versus Original's 5.
Neither page uses inline SVGs. Social and other icons are raster images or glyphs.

Both pages use class-based CSS with no utility framework (tailwind_like_fraction 0). Original is CMS-like, with 112 unique classes over 267 usages, 13 inline styles, 3 stylesheets, 32 scripts and a generator meta tag. The AI-built page is lighter, with 32 unique classes over 54 usages, 1 inline style, 1 stylesheet and 0 scripts.
Original lays out with flexbox only (10 elements, grid 0). The AI-built page uses flexbox (17 elements) and CSS grid (4 elements).

Both pages are short and image- and module-led, with similar word counts and no emoji, exclamation marks or em dashes. Original is 1894px tall with 168 words. The AI-built page is 2199px tall with 171 words.

Vertical spacing differs. Original leaves large blank orange gaps (~80–90px) between floating modules. The AI-built page runs contiguous full-width bands with regular ~40–48px section padding and its h2s aligned at x=186.

Original's title is a long brand string with a trailing pipe ('New Climate Economy | Commission on the Economy and Climate |'), plus legacy mobile meta tags (MobileOptimized, HandheldFriendly, cleartype). The AI-built page's title is just 'New Climate Economy' and its only meta tags are charset, viewport and description.

Link styling varies by context on the AI-built page: dark bold nav links, green bold section links, underlined green inline links and an underlined white footer link. On Original, links are mostly orange on white, with white nav links.
